subject: Request: exception for runtime analytics subprocessor & data-use redline
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@acme.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ben.thomas@acme.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exception for runtime analytics subprocessor & proposed redline

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for last week's demo. To move forward with procurement our security team at Acme needs a limited exception in section 5 (Data Use / Subprocessors) to allow sending anonymized runtime telemetry to our analytics partner, PrismMetrics. The ask is narrow — aggregated usage metrics and event-level counts derived from inference calls (no raw customer prompts or identifiable outputs).

Attached is our proposed redline (ACME_Redline_v3.pdf) and a small dataflow diagram showing where PrismMetrics would receive batched telemetry. Our procurement team has asked for Product and Security confirmation that:

- Redwood can support a subprocessor carveout limited to aggregated metrics (no token-level exports)
- Data sent can be pre-aggregated and sampled on Redwood's side before export
- PrismMetrics will be required to be SOC 2 Type II and sign a subprocessor addendum

We need a signoff or list of required changes by EOD Friday so we can keep the vendor timeline. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Sara Khan
Legal Counsel, Acme Corp

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: exception for runtime analytics subprocessor & proposed redline

Mateo / all — thanks for the ping and the attachments. Quick security assessment (high level) below. I also annotated ACME_Redline_v3.pdf with inline comments — see drive link in related_links.

Key concerns:
- "Aggregated metrics" is acceptable in principle, but the redline as written leaves the door open to exporting small-group aggregates or low-cardinality event sets that could be reconstructed. We need explicit constraints: minimum aggregation window (e.g., >= 1,000 events) and a prohibition on export of any fields that could be correlated back to a user or session id.
- We must explicitly prohibit exporting any token-level data, embeddings, or raw outputs. The clause should call out "no PII, no prompts, no generated output, nor token-level telemetry".
- Require PrismMetrics to be SOC 2 Type II and to sign Redwood's standard Subprocessor Agreement; include a clause for on-demand audit rights for security incidents.
- We should add a technical requirement: all telemetry leaving Redwood's runtime must be pre-processed server-side to remove any identifiers and aggregated according to a defined sample/aggregation policy. We should also log exports and surface them in Customer-facing audit logs (so Acme can see what was exported and when).

Suggested next steps:
1) Legal to propose concrete redline language that limits exports to "aggregated, non-identifiable metrics" with numeric thresholds for aggregation or sampling.
2) Product to confirm feasibility of server-side pre-aggregation and whether it impacts latency or instrumentation guarantees. If not feasible, we need to propose an alternative (e.g., offline batch export from customer-configured telemetry pipeline).
3) If Product confirms feasibility, Security will provide the exact technical constraints to include in the clause.

I do not recommend agreeing to any wording that could be interpreted to allow export of query-level telemetry or raw outputs.

- Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: Suggested_aggregation_thresholds (see Suggested_Clause_5.2_redline.docx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: exception for runtime analytics subprocessor & proposed redline

Thanks — I reviewed the ACME redline and Olga's notes. Draft position below we can send as a counter:

- We can accept an exception limited to aggregated, non-identifiable metrics. The clause must: 
  * Define "aggregated, non-identifiable metrics" as metrics that are both (a) aggregated across no fewer than 1,000 distinct inference events and (b) do not contain any user or session identifiers, prompts, prompt fragments, outputs, token-level data, or embeddings.
  * Require PrismMetrics to execute Redwood's Subprocessor Agreement and maintain SOC 2 Type II.
  * Require that all telemetry is pre-processed and sampled by Redwood prior to export; Redwood will retain export logs and make an export activity report available to Acme on request.
  * Prohibit any downstream use for model training without a separate written agreement.

Questions for Product (Laura):
- Can Redwood implement the server-side aggregation threshold (1,000 events) and sampling in a way that meets Acme's analytics needs? If not, please state: (a) the minimum viable aggregation window we can support, and (b) whether this must be implemented in the runtime (real-time) or can be satisfied with nearline/offline batch exports.

If Product confirms the above, Legal will prepare a concise counterproposal and updated clause language. Olga — we'll keep your audit and logging asks in the draft.

Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
